items.title: Reported barriers never linked to recorded attendance
items.whyItMatters: Without linkage, a survey describes the women who reply, mostly attenders (claim c5).
items.opportunity: Link survey answers to the booking record with consent, and describe non-respondents from records.

items.title: Non-attenders reply least
items.whyItMatters: Non-attenders replied at less than half the rate of attenders in the retrieved survey.
items.opportunity: Two reminders, a telephone option and a short form; compare respondents with non-respondents on recorded factors.

items.title: Women needing an interpreter
items.whyItMatters: They attend about half as often (claim c4) and an English-only survey would miss them.
items.opportunity: Translate the survey into the two most common other languages and offer an interpreter-supported telephone option.

items.title: Timing and childcare as modifiable factors
items.whyItMatters: They are the barriers a redesign could change (claims c2 and c3).
items.opportunity: Ask about preferred times, online classes and childcare in the survey.

errorsFound: The need treats the survey and the records review as alternatives; the question needs the records for every referral and the survey for barriers, joined for respondents.
reevaluation: The gaps point to one cross-sectional study of all women referred in a year: recorded factors for everyone, a translated survey of barriers, and linkage of the two where women agree.
summary: Four gaps; missing linkage, nonresponse and language are high severity.
